question: What accounts for the multi-chunk packed slot-local prefill slowdown (67 tok/s at 8 chunks vs the scalar parent's 692), now that the per-slab KV import is removed and proven not to be it?
answer: The native paged prefill attention kernel. qwen35_paged_full_attn_prefill_gqa_gate_bf16_kernel is 91% of prefill device time at 8 chunks (110.989 of 121.385 s), while every other kernel family (WMMA projections, GDN, norm, MoE, embedding) stays flat at ~1.25-1.34 s per slab. Its per-launch cost grows ~quadratically with the slab's end context (33.7 ms at ctx 1024 -> 3,042.1 ms at ctx 8192, ~90x for 8x context) where the algorithmic requirement is linear (rows x context). The route is 99.6% device-bound (121.385 s device time vs 121.86 s uninstrumented wall), so this is kernel efficiency, not host overhead and not copies.

protocol.profiler_recipe: cache-only, per benchmarks/HARNESSES.md: HIPENGINE_COMPILER_VERSION_FILE=/tmp/hipcc-version.txt and HIPENGINE_REQUIRE_CACHED_BUILD=1 (bare rocprofv3 attempts stall in hipcc --version compiler discovery under the profiler)
protocol.analysis: kernel trace segmented on embedding launches (one per slab); per-slab per-family device-time rollup; attention kernel identified by name
protocol.kv: int8_per_token_head, FP32 per-token/head scales, max_sequence_length 16384 (route int8_direct, slot-local full attention, AOTriton hard-disabled on transient-oracle layers)
protocol.cross_check: 2048-row (2-chunk) profile of the same protocol reproduces the slab-1/slab-2 per-launch costs (33.7 / 89.9 ms) and shows the same flat non-attention floor (~1.23 s/slab); decode steps cost ~0.03 s each

evidence.per_launch_growth_note: 33.7 -> 3042.1 ms over 8x context = ~90x, i.e. ~context^2 where the requirement is linear; total attention is then ~cubic in chunk count at fixed chunk size, matching the observed 6.8x wall from 4 to 8 chunks

mechanism.shape: one block per (q_head, query row) (blockIdx.x/y); each block serially walks the whole visible context with threads = 32 (ctx<=1024) or 64
mechanism.score_storage: dynamic LDS sized (max_context_len + threads + head_dim) * 4 bytes by the launcher (paged_attn_decode.py qwen35_paged_full_attn_prefill_gqa_gate_bf16_spans): ~4.6 KB at ctx 1024 -> ~33.5 KB at ctx 8192 per block, so wave occupancy collapses as the slab's end context grows; the serial page-walk then cannot hide latency
escape_hatches: AOTriton admission on transient-oracle layers (built, default OFF; its 2026-09-09 gate ran on the corrupted multi-chunk history and must be re-qualified on the corrected route)
the WMMA score-GEMM approach the scalar parent's bulk path already uses

not_a_perf_claim: No code changed in this measurement; the numbers attribute the existing slowdown.
